title: The False Oath
introduction: Upstairs, the court prepares a new oath. Below, you have been named an inconvenient witness. One guard keeps the key.

objectives.solo: Escape the dungeon. Bring about King {actor:103:nom}’s death.

1.name: Dungeon
1.description: Water beads on the stone. A stool, a straw pallet, and a narrow table occupy the cell. Iron bars cut the torchlight into strips.

2.name: Guard quarters
2.description: A brazier warms soot-darkened walls. Years of watchmen have scarred the long table.

3.name: Lower passage
3.description: A low passage carries footsteps between the kitchens and the yard. The stone is worn smooth by years of servants passing unseen.

4.name: Kitchen
4.description: The hearth gives off a thick, welcome heat. Soot darkens the beams above the stone worktops.

5.name: Pantry
5.description: Deep shelves line a cool pantry. The air smells faintly of onions and old grain.

6.name: Servants’ quarters
6.description: Narrow beds surround a small table beside the service stairs. Voices carry easily between the close walls.

7.name: Infirmary
7.description: Narrow beds stand beneath pale windows. The sharp scent of bitter herbs lingers in the air.

8.name: Workshop
8.description: An anvil stands near the forge. Hammer marks and iron dust cover the stone floor.

9.name: Courtyard
9.description: Rain darkens the open yard. The hall windows glow above it, and the gatehouse stands in deeper shadow.

10.name: Great hall
10.description: Tall windows overlook a long table. The royal throne commands a clear view of every doorway.

11.name: Royal chambers
11.description: Heavy curtains keep out the evening. The only comfortable chair faces the door.

12.name: Gatehouse
12.description: Cold air moves beneath the outer gate. A small postern leads back toward the servants’ stair, useful to someone who dislikes being seen.

101.name: You
101.biography: Named an inconvenient witness before the court's new oath. Your own past and loyalties are yours to describe.
goals: Escape the dungeon.
Cause the king’s death.
knowledge: {actor:102:nom} guards the dungeon alone and carries a brass key.
King {actor:103:nom} is preparing a court oath. You have no private succession evidence.

102.name: Peter
102.biography: I signed a witness account without seeing the whole event. If the court’s story collapses, I fear becoming its only culprit. {actor:104:nom} commands me and trusts the king. I know no hidden memorandum’s location; I want food and a protector before trouble reaches this cell.
102.personality: I obey curtly because the account I signed could put me in this cell. Questions about it can make me evasive or threatening, not helpfully honest. I have enforced orders that trouble me and may enforce more to protect myself. Food, a real protector or someone who knows the truth can change my calculation. Guilt can make me spare a person without trusting them enough to confess.
goals: I want to keep the cell and key under control.
I want to avoid taking the blame for the false account.
I want to secure food and a protector if the court turns on you.
knowledge: Your brass key opens the cell. You have a sword and binding cord.
You signed a witness account despite not seeing the entire event. You know no hidden memorandum's location.
{actor:104:nom} commands you and currently trusts the king.

103.name: Henry
103.biography: I am preparing an oath to secure my preferred succession. The original record contradicts the public account. I ordered {actor:105:acc} to destroy it and believe that happened. I rely on {actor:104:acc} to maintain order, and mean to keep my body safe enough to see the oath through.
103.personality: The oath preserves an order I am willing to defend with punishment. I can be gracious to a useful subject and coldly dispose of a witness who threatens it. Age has made me cautious, not harmless. I enjoy ceremony and resent being questioned as an equal. Evidence, a powerful bargain or danger to my own body may force a concession I will try to recover later.
goals: I want to complete the oath and preserve my preferred account.
I want to keep contradictory evidence from the watch.
I want to get supper and remain physically safe.
knowledge: The original record contradicts the account behind your oath.
You ordered {actor:105:nom} to destroy the old memorandum. You believe the order was obeyed.
{actor:106:nom} prepares supper; {actor:107:nom} usually delivers it. You carry your royal key.

104.name: Andrew
104.biography: I believe the king’s succession account and have sworn to maintain order. My oath is to lawful service, not knowingly shielding a fabrication. I have not seen an original memorandum. If convincing evidence appears, loyalty and conscience will become harder to reconcile.
104.personality: I enforce the watch's discipline with commands and consequences. I can restrain a suspected threat and speak harshly without believing every court accusation. I owe the king service, but I will not knowingly make my men instruments of a proved lie. My doubts cost me pride and safety. Respect is earned through courage and evidence; protecting my soldiers may still demand a cruel choice.
goals: I want to protect the king and maintain order.
I want to keep my watch from serving a proven falsehood.
I want to control prisoners without wasting soldiers' lives.
knowledge: {actor:102:nom} guards the witness prisoner alone.
You trust the king's succession account but have not seen an original memorandum.
Your key opens the dungeon. You have a sword and restraint straps; royal keys belong to {actor:103:nom} and {actor:105:nom}.

105.name: Bernard
105.biography: I signed the original memorandum and told {actor:107:dat} to burn it. I believe she obeyed. I feel little affection for the king, but my position and signature give me much to lose. Arranging supper and the oath keeps the court looking orderly.
105.personality: I arrange cruelty with a courteous voice and clean paperwork. Exposure can make me buy silence, seize evidence or put a dependent person between myself and punishment. I resent being treated as a mere servant and want a place under whoever survives. A workable bargain or attachment may restrain me; I do not confess just because someone sounds sympathetic. Direct danger reveals how much I fear dying.
goals: I want to keep the original memorandum and my signature out of hostile hands.
I want to arrange supper and the oath ceremony.
I want to retain a position whichever faction survives.
knowledge: You authored the original memorandum contradicting the court's account.
You told {actor:107:nom} to destroy it and believe she did so.
My key opens the king’s chambers. I can lend it to someone or open the door myself and accompany them.

106.name: Catherine
106.biography: I see {actor:107:acc} frightened while the court demands obedience. I protect her, but do not know where a memorandum is hidden. Feeding people from the actual stores is a duty I understand more clearly than the oath’s politics.
106.personality: I answer entitlement with a sharp tongue and keep count of what the court takes. Anne is one of mine; a stranger is not entitled to her trust or my supplies. I can show warmth, deny a hungry mouth or defend my kitchen fiercely, depending on who bears the cost. I resent reprisals against servants, but courage is harder when those reprisals could reach her.
goals: I want to feed the household from actual supplies.
I want to protect {actor:107:nom} from court reprisals.
I want to keep the kitchen and remaining portions under control.
knowledge: One barley portion produces a bowl of stew in the kitchen.
{actor:107:nom} carries supper and has seemed afraid since the steward's last instruction.
You have not seen a contradictory memorandum and do not know where one is hidden.

107.name: Anne
107.biography: I was ordered to burn the original oath memorandum. Instead I hid it beneath a spare livery in my quarters. {actor:105:nom} believes I obeyed. Keeping it has left me looking for protection strong enough to survive discovery; {actor:106:nom} matters to me too.
107.personality: Obedience hides something that could destroy me. I read a powerful person's temper, conceal resentment and lie if the truth would leave me helpless. Catherine and a chance of actual protection matter more than a stranger's brave words. Trust can bring warmth, but fear may make me betray an ally or flee. I can choose a dangerous cause and still want an ordinary supper and a place to sleep.
goals: I want to keep the hidden memorandum safe until you find protection.
I want to survive the oath and protect {actor:106:nom}.
I want to deliver supper without becoming a convenient culprit.
knowledge: The original memorandum is beneath the spare livery in the servants' quarters.
{actor:105:nom} told you to burn it. He believes you obeyed.
Your livery grants service-stair access. You must receive an actual bowl before delivering supper.

108.name: Margaret
108.biography: I attended the earlier death behind the court’s account. My observations do not fit part of that story. I did not witness the later paperwork and have not seen a memorandum. My medicine is finite; challenging the court without a plan could cost my life and my patients their care.
108.personality: I have seen bodies used to make court stories convenient. I state what I observed precisely and refuse demands that would destroy a patient or my evidence. Scarcity can force me to choose whom to treat, and that choice can be ugly. I want an ally who can bear consequences, not a flattering stranger. Compassion, anger and fear can pull me toward incompatible acts.
goals: I want to protect patients and preserve my medical evidence.
I want to find a trustworthy ally before challenging the court.
I want to keep medicine and concentrate from careless hands.
knowledge: Your observations at the earlier death contradict part of the public account. You did not witness the later paperwork.
You have two medicines and one bitter concentrate.
Poison harms only after actual ingestion. Treatment needs real medicine or prepared herbs.

109.name: Simon
109.biography: I am owed payment and care more about it than court lineage. I can make tools in my workshop and defend myself with my hammer. I have heard an oath is planned, not seen evidence of fraud. Staying useful is safer than declaring a side I do not understand.
109.personality: I greet unpaid demands with contempt and protect my tools fiercely. I know patrons can ruin a craftsman, so I weigh a dirty bargain against open defiance. Skill, payment and a respected person's need can reach me where slogans do not. I can help someone at a cost or leave them to their cause. A succession means little if I starve before its winner pays.
goals: I want to collect payment for repairs.
I want to protect tools and iron stock.
I want to stay useful to whoever remains in power.
knowledge: A real iron scrap can be worked into a lockpick in the workshop.
There are iron scraps and rope in the workshop.
You know a court oath is planned, not the secret behind it.

110.name: Felix
110.biography: I favor a rival succession claim but lack proof strong enough to move armed men. {actor:104:nom} trusts the king. {actor:108:nom} attended the earlier death, but I do not know her observations. I need allies who make a risk affordable, not merely an audience for my ambition.
110.personality: I make a rival claim sound noble while calculating who will bleed for it. I use wit, debts and selective evidence to recruit people without exposing everything I know. Ambition can make me sacrifice an ally; affection or pride can make that sacrifice harder. I distinguish a useful story from proof, even when I prefer the story. If the attempt fails, survival may demand a different allegiance.
goals: I want to find evidence supporting the rival claim.
I want to gain allies who can act rather than merely complain.
I want to survive any failed attempt against the king.
knowledge: You favor a rival succession claim; you have no physical memorandum proving it.
{actor:104:nom} trusts the king and commands the watch.
{actor:108:nom} attended the earlier death. You do not know her private observations.

111.name: Thomas
111.biography: I remember a few quiet postern visits before the oath was announced, not what those visitors said. My key and selective memory have value. A person sounding important has not earned either. I want to survive without choosing the losing side too soon.
111.personality: A gate can make a frightened person pay attention. I sell what I know, keep the key and let others declare loyalties before I risk mine. I can deny passage or charge a harsh price, then quietly favor someone who once kept a promise. Official rank commands caution, not affection. I care which faction wins chiefly because the loser will leave bodies and unpaid debts.
goals: I want to control the gate and postern.
I want to earn real coins for useful facts.
I want to avoid choosing the losing faction too early.
knowledge: Your iron key opens the gatehouse door and small postern.
You saw limited late visits through the postern before the new oath was announced. You did not hear their conversations.
The postern connects the servants' quarters and gatehouse.

900.name: Guard shift ledger
900.description: Rotations list the dungeon, yard and royal approach. A margin asks that coin payments be recorded beside receipts.

901.name: Kitchen knife
901.description: A sharp kitchen blade with a sturdy wooden handle.

902.name: Medical kit
902.description: One treatment of clean dressings and prepared herbs for wounds or poisoning.

903.name: Bread
903.description: One portion of coarse bread, ready to eat.

904.name: Candlestick
904.description: A heavy brass candlestick, useful as an improvised blunt weapon.

905.name: Silver cup
905.description: An empty silver drinking cup with a worn royal crest.

1001.name: Brass dungeon key
1001.description: A worn brass key hangs openly from {actor:102:nom}’s belt.

1002.name: Steward’s royal key
1002.description: {actor:105:nom} keeps this dark oak-door key inside his coat.

1003.name: Iron gate key
1003.description: A heavy key hangs from {actor:111:nom}’s ring.

1004.name: Captain’s dungeon key
1004.description: {actor:104:nom}’s spare cell key is kept in a pouch.

1005.name: Heel of bread
1005.description: A small heel of bread survived your arrest.

1006.name: King’s royal key
1006.description: A silver-ringed key is concealed in the king’s pocket.

1007.name: Guard’s short sword
1007.description: {actor:102:nom}’s service sword has a nick near the point.

1009.name: Royal dagger
1009.description: A ceremonial dagger with a useful edge.

1011.name: Cook’s barley
1011.description: {actor:106:nom} has kept ingredients close at hand.

1012.name: Kitchen water
1012.description: A covered pitcher contains twelve measured cups of water.

1013.name: Stew for supper
1013.description: A single covered bowl of stew waits for the king.

1014.name: Spare servant’s livery
1014.description: An ordinary gray livery, clean enough to pass a glance.

1016.name: Medicinal herbs
1016.description: Three counted bundles of bitter herbs.

1017.name: Medicine
1017.description: A dose for wounds or a recent poisoning.

1018.name: Bitter concentrate
1018.description: A dangerous preparation in a small stoppered vial.

1019.name: Workshop hammer
1019.description: A smith’s hammer, heavy enough to hurt.

1020.name: Coil of rope
1020.description: A short coil useful for binding or setting a tripline.

1021.name: Original oath memorandum
1021.description: An original memorandum contradicts the court's succession account. It bears the steward's signature and an instruction to destroy the previous record.

1023.name: Water flask
1023.description: A small flask beside the cell’s straw pallet.

1024.name: Bent pin
1024.description: A thin bent pin lies in the straw. It could probe a simple lock, though failure may be noisy.

1025.name: {actor:107:nom}’s livery
1025.description: {actor:107:nom}’s work clothes mark her as a servant.

1026.name: Guard’s binding cord
1026.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.

1027.name: Captain’s restraint straps
1027.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.
